findings.title: CANCEL (and REJECTED) reply can now arrive after the caller's receive deadline when freezing is slow
findings.scenario: run_broker.cancel sends CANCEL with until <= now+1 s. If a unit does not report frozen==1 within that window, the HEAD helper replied CANCELLED(reason 6, partial mask) by until; the new helper keeps waiting up to min(generation, now+2 s). The client raises ML-AFFA-TIMEOUT or ML-AFFA-LATE-ACK, revokes (SIGKILL of the authority), and RunCancellation is built from the revocation; no CANCELLED frame enters _epoch_history, so the terminal precondition (bootstrap.py:859-861, run_broker.py:858-863) depends on observed authority death and evidence.py:315 records nativeCancellationAcknowledged=false. The same applies to an early rejection whose REJECTED reply now follows a wait longer than the request remainder. Direction is conservative: the freeze writes were issued before the wait, the authority is killed, and the supervisor cleanup refreezes (bootstrap.c:258-277).
findings.recommendation: Record the trade-off in the review log, or bound the CANCEL wait by the request deadline (now sufficient for F-01 because the write is unconditional) while keeping close_end for the rejection path; in either case state which reply-timing guarantee the CANCEL receipt carries.

findings.title: Freeze writes are serialised behind each unit's wait; units after an exhausted budget are never read
findings.scenario: freeze_all writes unit i and waits for it before writing unit i+1. One unit that does not freeze consumes the whole 2 s budget, delaying the freeze write of every later unit (which may host a released, running workload) by up to 2 s. Units reached after the budget is exhausted get the write but no read (frozen stays 0, the loop at 164 is not entered), so they are excluded from the mask and set freeze_failed even if already frozen, yielding reason 6 / exit 70 spuriously.
findings.recommendation: Use two passes: issue every cgroup.freeze write first, then wait for frozen==1 under the shared budget, reading each unit at least once (do-while) so the mask is not under-reported.

findings.title: Prior F-01 recommendation to retry pending freezes in the closed loop is neither implemented nor recorded as deferred
findings.scenario: After a close whose freeze could not be confirmed, the closed authority keeps serving cleanup-only requests until generation-2 s without re-issuing the freeze, unless a later CANCEL or cleanup() calls close_authority again. Findings 394/395 do not mention this part of the prior recommendation.
findings.recommendation: Either implement a bounded retry for units not in the last mask or record the item as deferred/declined with rationale in review-affa18.md.

findings.title: A failed reply send can now trigger up to three successive 2 s close budgets
findings.scenario: If the CANCELLED send at 395 fails (MSG_DONTWAIT, peer gone), command returns -1, main re-runs close_authority with a fresh close_end (520), then a failed REJECTED send leads to cleanup() with another min(generation, now+2 s). Worst case about 6 s when units do not freeze, always bounded by g->generation; the second close previously had an elapsed budget and returned quickly. Fail-safe; the supervisor watchdog is independent.
findings.recommendation: Optional: return cleanup(g) directly when a reply send fails, or skip the re-close when the authority is already closed and the last mask was complete.

findings.title: Close activity can extend into the last 2 s of the generation and leave cleanup() an elapsed budget
findings.scenario: A close started near generation-2 s may run until the generation; the next loop iteration (500) calls cleanup(), whose end = min(generation, now+2 s) can already be <= now. With this change cleanup still issues the freeze writes, but performs no frozen wait and no kills (472 requires now < generation), and returns 70. The authority never acts past the generation beyond loop granularity, and the wire constraint until <= generation-2 s is unaffected.
findings.recommendation: None required; document that the authority's close and the supervisor cleanup may overlap in [generation-2 s, generation].

findings.title: write_freeze()==1 (ENOENT/ENODEV) counted as freeze failure, unlike bootstrap.c
findings.scenario: A removed cgroup that removed() does not recognise (errno other than ENOENT on any of the three controls) reaches write_freeze, which returns 1; freeze_all sets freeze_failed (reason 6 / exit 70), whereas bootstrap.c:265/271 treat 1 as resolved. Pre-existing, conservative, and unchanged in outcome by this diff; no write can reach a removed or different cgroup.
findings.recommendation: Optional: treat write_freeze()==1 as removed (set the mask bit) for consistency with bootstrap.c, or record the stricter semantics.

findings.title: Fence-control docstring is stale and the control cannot exercise the new FREEZE_FAILED or bounded-wait branches
findings.scenario: The docstring still says the native authority skips its refreeze and that there are no helper byte changes, contradicting helper_bytes_changed=True (84). Because the ancestor freeze keeps the unit frozen, frozen==1 is observed immediately, so the control covers the unconditional write but neither the budgeted wait nor the REJECTED reason 6 path; line 64 would fail first if the refreeze were unconfirmed.
findings.recommendation: Update the docstring; record that the FREEZE_FAILED branch and the bounded wait are untested, or add a control for them.

findings.title: Pre-existing timing details in the close paths (not introduced by this diff)
findings.scenario: (a) If clock_gettime fails, now_ns() returns 0, close_end returns g->generation and the wait loop 164 compares 0 < end, so the wait is unbounded while the clock keeps failing (same pattern as cleanup():468). (b) poll on g->parent at 166 returns immediately once the parent has exited, so the wait busy-spins for the budget. (c) After the lease-expiry close at 501 the poll timeout at 504 uses the pre-close now, delaying the generation-2 s cleanup trigger by up to the close duration (bounded by the generation).
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening: treat now_ns()==0 as budget exhausted inside the wait loops; recompute now after the lease-expiry close.

verdict_rationale: The cgroup.freeze write is issued for every live generation regardless of budget (162), the wait is bounded (164-167), and the rejection path (520) and CANCEL (394) use an independent min(generation, now+2 s) budget; cleanup() and the lease-expiry path already used fresh budgets. Residual items are LOW/NOTE and conservative in direction; the REJECTED freeze mask remains deferred with F-05.
